summary.intent: Diagnose and fix CI failures on PR #1117 caused by a `waitUntil` typing change in a service worker file, then verify the fix across all TS gates before re-pushing.
summary.outcome: Identified and fixed a TypeScript typing error where `waitUntil?` was incorrectly placed on `FetchEventLike` (which doesn't have that member) instead of the correct interface; re-ran typecheck/build gates unpiped to confirm real exit codes, then committed and pushed the fix.

repo: Service worker event interfaces in packages/client/src/sw/install.ts distinguish FetchEventLike from another interface that actually owns `waitUntil` — don't assume all SW event-like interfaces share the same optional members.

code.finding: `waitUntil?` was declared on `FetchEventLike`, which has no `waitUntil` member; it belongs on a different event interface. This caused 7 CI failures on PR #1117 that local typecheck missed.

workflow: Piping `tsc` (or any command) through `tail` for readability captures `tail`'s exit code in `$?`, not the piped command's — this silently masks real failures. Always run type/build gates unpiped to get accurate exit codes.
This exact piping mistake was one the user had already warned wave-6 agents about, yet still hit it themselves — worth calling out explicitly when scripting CI/local gate checks.

friction: Local typecheck falsely reported success because its exit code was silently overwritten by piping through `tail`, letting a real type error reach CI on PR #1117 (7 failures).
